2598e3c4-db86-44f8-ab96-6805525be1ac.title: Flight Software Engineering Intern
2598e3c4-db86-44f8-ab96-6805525be1ac.description:
About the role 
 The Flight Software team manages the software running on the Spark-1 flight computer and peripheral boards. This includes everything from command and telemetry handling to GNC execution, fault management, and the reentry sequence. You will own technical tasks and work with engineers across GNC, avionics, and mission operations to design, test, and operate our spacecraft. 
 What you'll do 
 
 Write flight software for Spark-1 in Rust and firmware for peripheral boards in C++. 
 Implement logic for GNC, power, thermal, and fault management based on analysis and simulation models. 
 Develop command and telemetry handling, packet definitions, sensor and actuator drivers, and ground decoding tools. 
 Build and maintain test infrastructure, including unit tests, software-in-the-loop and hardware-in-the-loop regression, and flatsat automation. 
 Support the integration and testing of flight software with avionics hardware and mission operations tools. 
 
 What you'll need 
 
 Current enrollment in a BS, MS, or PhD program in computer science, computer engineering, electrical engineering, or a related field. 
 Experience in embedded software, systems programming, real-time systems, or hardware interfacing through coursework, research, or projects. 
 Familiarity with Rust, C, C++, Python, Linux development, and git. 
 Ability to write software that communicates over interfaces like SPI, I2C, UART, CAN, or Ethernet and test it against real hardware. 
 Preferred experience includes at least one year on a technical project team like a CubeSat, Rocket Team, or Formula SAE group. 
 Bonus points for experience with flight software for spacecraft or robotics, embedded Rust, embedded Linux, RTOS environments, SoC platforms like Zynq UltraScale+, or frameworks such as F Prime or cFS. 
 Strong communication and technical documentation skills. 
 
 Location & details 
 
 This is an on-site internship based in San Francisco, California. 
 We are hiring for the Winter 2027 and Summer 2027 terms. Please indicate which term you are applying for in your application. 
 This is a paid, full-time position. 
 Due to U.S. export control requirements, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or permanent resident. We do not provide visa sponsorship.

You will own projects that ship, rather than working on side tasks. We prioritize evidence over assumptions and value independent verification of results. You should be comfortable reporting failures early and working with physical hardware. 
 What you'll do 
 
 Build data collection tools, including teleop capture, episode management, and labeling pipelines. 
 Develop training and evaluation infrastructure, such as reproducible runs, checkpoint management, and evaluation harnesses. 
 Work on imitation learning, visual servoing, and observation-space design. 
 Manage perception tasks by using segmentation and tracking models to feed structured observations to controllers. 
 Deploy policies onto real hardware and ensure they run reliably at control frequencies. 
 Perform maintenance tasks like fixing data loaders, chasing timing mismatches, and re-cutting fixtures. 
 Monitor hardware cells during failure testing. 
 
 What you'll need 
 
 Strong Python skills and experience writing code for others to maintain. 
 Comfort with PyTorch and the ability to debug training loops. 
 Proficiency in Linux and git. 
 Empirical instincts to isolate variables when troubleshooting. 
 Current enrollment in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, robotics, or a related field, or equivalent demonstrated skill.

 Modality: On-site. 
 Term: Rolling. 
 Employment type: Full-time. 
 Compensation: $20 - $60 per month.

5a193e01-5485-4cce-b2b1-b02d93cbf042.description:
About the role 
 Teaching a 40-ton excavator to operate like an expert is a unique challenge. Unlike autonomous cars, these machines require multimodal motions where multiple approaches to digging or dumping are valid. The Behavior ML team develops the learned policies that guide these machines. We use diffusion policies to represent the full distribution of expert behavior rather than averaging it. As an intern, you will train these policies and help build the evaluation frameworks that determine their performance. 
 What you'll do 
 
 Train and iterate on diffusion-based behavior policies using real fleet demonstration data and simulated rollouts. 
 Run architecture, conditioning, and hyperparameter explorations to produce clear findings for the team. 
 Build and improve evaluation pipelines that score behavior models. 
 Investigate failure modes such as distribution shift, mode collapse, and out-of-distribution scenes. 
 Propose fixes for model failure modes. 
 Work with simulation and evaluation teams to correlate offline metrics with on-machine performance. 
 Contribute to the shared training codebase with clean, reviewed, and reproducible work. 
 Share results regularly with the behavior, controls, and autonomy teams. 
 
 What you'll need 
 
 Currently pursuing a BS, MS, or PhD in computer science, robotics, machine learning, or a related field, or have equivalent research or industry experience.

a608ed4e-05a8-499e-95be-db5f7db34ba5.title: Internship Simulation Engineer, Neural Rendering
a608ed4e-05a8-499e-95be-db5f7db34ba5.description:
About the role 
 Before an autonomous excavator digs its first trench on a new site, it has already dug thousands in simulation. The Simulation team builds the virtual environments our autonomy stack trains and tests against. Neural rendering is the next step. We are replacing hand-authored assets with learned representations that capture the visual complexity of real jobsites, such as dust, lighting, and deformable terrain. As our Simulation intern, you will push neural rendering techniques into our pipeline and measure whether they close the visual gap for downstream autonomy performance. 
 What you'll do 
 
 Research, implement, and benchmark neural rendering methods like NeRF or 3D Gaussian splatting for generating realistic construction-site imagery. 
 Train models on real-world site data captured by our fleet and evaluate visual fidelity, render speed, and temporal consistency. 
 Integrate neural rendering outputs into the simulation pipeline to support perception and planning teams. 
 Build evaluation metrics and tooling that quantify how well rendered scenes match real fleet data and whether that improvement transfers to autonomy performance. 
 Identify and address failure modes including dynamic objects, deformable terrain, dust, and harsh lighting. 
 Document findings, limitations, and recommendations on where neural rendering should replace traditional sim assets. 
 
 What you'll need 
 
 Currently pursuing a BS, MS, or PhD in computer science, computer graphics, robotics, or a related field, or equivalent research or industry experience. 
 Strong Python skills and hands-on experience with PyTorch or equivalent frameworks. 
 Solid understanding of 3D graphics fundamentals, including rendering pipelines, scene representations, camera models, and coordinate systems. 
 Familiarity with neural scene representations such as NeRF or Gaussian splatting. 
 Comfort working with real-world data from construction sites. 
 Published work or project experience in neural rendering, novel view synthesis, or differentiable rendering is preferred. 
 Experience with simulation engines like Unreal, Unity, or NVIDIA Isaac Sim. 
 Background in autonomous vehicle simulation or synthetic data generation. 
 Familiarity with C++ and GPU programming including CUDA, OpenGL, or Vulkan. 
 
 Location & details 
 
 Location: San Francisco, California 
 Term: Summer 2027 
 Modality: On-site 
 Employment: Full-time internship 
 Compensation: Paid position

c660ae47-5011-4e9c-9fc9-da62e5c35927.description:
About the role 
 This is a research-engineering internship for individuals operating at or near the post-doctoral level. You will shape the architecture of a multi-target joint probabilistic foundation model designed to solve complex real-world problems. The project focuses on building a system capable of temporal forecasting, unordered tabular regression, classification, and missing-data completion while maintaining coherent joint structure across variables and scenarios. We prioritize creating real value in serious use cases over isolated benchmark optimization. 
 What you'll do 
 
 Design and improve core model architecture, including input encoders for temporal and tabular data, attention mechanisms, and distributional output heads. 
 Implement, train, and evaluate PyTorch models within a production-quality codebase. 
 Run controlled architecture studies, such as ablations, scaling behavior, and throughput profiling, to inform design decisions. 
 Build scalable PyTorch implementations that optimize for memory and throughput.

 Experience with version control, code review, testing, debugging, or open-source projects.

1774f645-5066-493a-aa21-5a5d27700bc1.description:
About the role 
 The American Heart Association is seeking an intern to support the Data Science team. This role focuses on machine learning and artificial intelligence, specifically large language models (LLMs), generative AI, and agentic AI. You will build foundational knowledge of how LLMs function and apply them to modeling, analytical workflows, and research use cases. Working alongside data scientists and cross-functional partners, you will help develop reproducible AI-enabled workflows and learn to evaluate, validate, and document solutions for clinical and biomedical research settings. 
 What you'll do 
 
 Support the design and development of LLM-powered applications and agentic AI workflows for clinical, biomedical, and operational research. 
 Apply LLMs to modeling and analytical tasks such as information extraction, classification, summarization, question answering, and workflow orchestration. 
 Experiment with prompt design, structured outputs, retrieval-augmented generation, embeddings, vector search, tool use, and multi-step agent workflows. 
 Prepare, clean, organize, and document data used in LLM and generative AI experiments. 
 Develop reproducible prototypes and workflows using Python and approved AI/ML tools. 
 Design and perform evaluations of LLM systems using quantitative and qualitative measures. 
 Conduct validation, error analysis, robustness testing, and comparison of model or workflow alternatives. 
 Assess issues including hallucination, factual consistency, relevance, reliability, bias, privacy, and reproducibility. 
 Document methods, assumptions, prompts, evaluation results, limitations, and recommended improvements. 
 Contribute to technical documentation, presentations, abstracts, manuscripts, and project discussions. 
 
 What you'll need 
 
 Currently pursuing an MS or PhD in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Biomedical Informatics, Data Science, Statistics, Engineering, Public Health, or a related quantitative field. 
 Coursework or project experience with LLMs, generative AI, natural language processing, retrieval-augmented generation, or AI agents. 
 Experience using APIs or open-source frameworks to build and test LLM applications. 
 Programming experience in Python and familiarity with common data analysis or machine learning libraries. 
 Ability to understand and apply core LLM concepts such as tokens, context windows, embeddings, prompting, retrieval, and generation. 
 Strong analytical, problem-solving, organizational, and attention-to-detail skills. 
 Commitment to reproducible research, responsible AI practices, data quality, and clear documentation. 
 Ability to communicate effectively and collaborate with technical and non-technical colleagues. 
 Experience working with cloud computing or high-performance computing environments (e.g., AWS, Snowflake, Azure, GCP). 
 Familiarity with model evaluation, experimental design, error analysis, version control, or reproducible workflow practices. 
 Intermediate to excellent proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook, and PowerPoint. 
 Experience with healthcare, clinical, or biomedical datasets is preferred. 
 Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship. 
 
 Location & details 
 
 Term: Winter 2027 (January 25, 2027, to May 7, 2027). 
 Modality: Remote. 
 Compensation: $23.00 per hour. 
 Availability: Minimum of 20 hours per week, Monday through Friday, between 8:30am and 5:00pm. 
 Equipment: Reliable WiFi connection required.

 Exposure to multi-modal/VLA models or robotics frameworks is also preferred.

 Employment Type: Full-time intern.

 Use simulation tools to evaluate perception models and overall system performance. 
 Write, debug, and deploy software components for robotic systems within a Linux and ROS environment. 
 Document test results and share findings with the engineering team. 
 Support the evaluation and benchmarking of perception sensors. 
 
 What you'll need 
 
 Current enrollment in a bachelor or master degree program in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Robotics, or a related field.

 Development experience in Linux (Ubuntu) and familiarity with ROS.

 Strong problem-solving and debugging skills.

 This is an on-site role based in Bedford, Massachusetts.

About the role 
 As an Embedded Software Engineering Intern, you will help build the systems powering Northwood ground stations. You will work alongside hardware, firmware, and software engineers to develop and test embedded platforms. This role offers hands-on experience with embedded Linux, hardware interfaces, and system-level development. You will own an internship project and present your work at the end of the term. 
 What you'll do 
 
 Develop and test software for Linux-based embedded devices. 
 Contribute to embedded Linux tooling, system configuration, and user-space applications. 
 Help develop and improve over-the-air software update capabilities. 
 Debug software and hardware integration issues alongside firmware and hardware engineers. 
 Work with hardware communication interfaces like I2C, SPI, UART, and USB. 
 Use laboratory equipment such as oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, and multimeters to troubleshoot systems. 
 Write tests and documentation to improve the reliability and maintainability of embedded systems. 
 Collaborate with FPGA, electrical, firmware, and software engineers on system integration. 
 
 What you'll need 
 
 Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field. 
 Experience programming in C, C++, Rust, or Python. 
 Familiarity with Linux environments and command-line tools. 
 Understanding of fundamental computer architecture and operating system concepts. 
 Familiarity with embedded systems, microcontrollers, or hardware-software interaction. 
 Ability to work collaboratively in a hands-on engineering environment. 
 To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, you must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident, or a protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3). 
 
 Location & details 
 
 Location: Los Angeles, California. 
 Term: Summer 2027. 
 Modality: On-site, full-time. 
 Compensation: This is a paid internship.

Instead, you will work to identify how automated scripts bypass browser-level defenses and invent new signals to stop them. The goal is to produce original research and validate your findings against real customer data. If your signals prove effective, they will be integrated into the BrowserGuard product by our engineering team. 
 What you'll do 
 
 Study how browser-based bots evade detection by working closely with Chromium and JavaScript internals. 
 Form and test original hypotheses to produce net-new detection signals. 
 Validate your ideas against real customer data to ensure they catch bots without flagging real users. 
 Hand off your best signals to the engineering team for implementation. 
 Engage in high-value projects outside the immediate scope of the role. 
 
 What you'll need 
 
 Master's or PhD-level computer science student, recent graduate, or equivalent depth. 
 Proven research instincts and experience working on problems where the answer was not known in advance. 
 Deep understanding of browser internals and knowledge of JavaScript from the inside. 
 Ability to learn Chromium internals and internet protocols. 
 Independent and curious mindset. 
 Bonus points for contributions to the Chromium project, open-source browser or security work, or prior research in bot detection, anti-fraud, anti-spoofing, or adversarial ML.

About the role 
 As a SEAM Intern, you will work on a research or engineering project focused on sensing, estimation, localization, mapping, or autonomy reliability. You will collaborate with engineers and researchers to design algorithms, implement software, and evaluate system performance in real-world autonomous driving systems. The State Estimation, Alignment, and Mapping (SEAM) team develops the sensing and spatial understanding capabilities that help autonomous vehicles interpret their surroundings and maintain reliable operation. 
 What you'll do 
 
 Develop, prototype, and evaluate algorithms for sensor fusion, state estimation, localization, calibration, and mapping. 
 Work with camera, lidar, radar, inertial, vehicle, map, and other multimodal data sources. 
 Implement software and tools for data processing, visualization, offline analysis, simulation, and system evaluation. 
 Analyze accuracy, robustness, latency, and failure modes across diverse operating conditions. 
 Apply software engineering best practices, including design reviews, code reviews, automated testing, continuous integration, and documentation. 
 Collaborate with perception, planning, controls, robotics, systems engineering, and vehicle-program partners. 
 Communicate technical findings and contribute to design discussions and project documentation. 
 
 What you'll need 
 
 Currently enrolled in or pursuing a Master’s or Ph.D. degree in Robotics, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or a related technical field. 
 Graduation date between December 2027 and June 2028. 
 Demonstrated experience through coursework, research, academic projects, or professional work in robotics, state estimation, sensor fusion, computer vision, localization, mapping, or controls. 
 Strong programming skills in C++ and/or Python. 
 Strong foundation in linear algebra, probability, geometry, optimization, or estimation methods. 
 Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. 
 Ability to work collaboratively in a cross-functional, team-oriented environment. 
 Strong written, verbal, and presentation skills. 
 Availability to work full-time, 40 hours per week, during the internship. 
 Experience with Kalman filtering, factor graphs, SLAM, visual-inertial odometry, bundle adjustment, point clouds, geometric computer vision, or multi-sensor calibration is preferred. 
 Familiarity with autonomous vehicles, ROS, machine learning frameworks like PyTorch or TensorFlow, and real-time or distributed systems is a plus. 
 Intent to return to a degree program after completion of the internship. 
 
 Location & details 
 
 Location: Sunnyvale, California. 
 Term: Summer 2027. 
 Work Modality: Hybrid (on-site 3 days a week). 
 Employment: Full-time, paid internship.
